comparison: Both evaluate the core mechanism of assembly formation through predictive plasticity (C4-C6, C75). OpenEval provides broader coverage including probabilistic replay claims (C17, C23-C26), while peer review focuses specifically on the predictive plasticity mechanism. Both find strong support with no concerns raised.

Both address the dual inhibitory plasticity mechanism (C21-C22, C65-C67, C76). OpenEval validates this through simplified and DL models, while peer review explicitly confirms both homeostatic and competitive inhibitory plasticity are required. Complete agreement on this key finding.

Both evaluate probability encoding through assembly activity and connectivity (C30-C36). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative linear relationships in Figure 3, while peer review confirms assembly wiring follows stimulus likelihood. Both find strong support with no disagreement.

Perfect overlap on synaptic weight encoding of probabilities (C37-C39). Both evaluations confirm that normalized excitatory weights match stimulus probabilities. Complete agreement with no concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect overlap on inhibitory plasticity necessity for stability (C41-C46). Both confirm ongoing inhibitory plasticity is required for maintaining learned representations. Complete agreement on this mechanism.

Perfect overlap on conditional probability learning (C50-C52). OpenEval validates hierarchical Bayesian computation capability, while peer review treats this as an accepted extension showing model versatility. Both supportive.

Both evaluate behavioral data matching (C53-C59, C94-C95). OpenEval emphasizes reproduction without curve fitting and acknowledges alternative mechanisms (C96). Peer review confirms the experimental link as a strength. Both supportive with appropriate caveats.

OpenEval addresses DL model implementation (C62-C70) while peer review focuses on dual inhibitory mechanism (C21-C22, C65-C67, C76). Partial overlap on inhibitory pathway division. Both supportive of the dual mechanism, though evaluating different aspects.

OpenEval evaluates DL model and ablation studies (C62-C64, C70, C40), while peer review treats these as confirmatory evidence for the dual inhibitory mechanism. Both supportive, viewing results as validation rather than primary contributions.

Both address mechanistic distinctions from prior models (C7, C18-C19, C88, C90-C91). OpenEval finds support through simulation evidence, but peer review raises significant concerns about novelty claims, noting Kappel et al. contradictions. Major disagreement on novelty characterization.

Perfect overlap on homeostatic mechanism (C84-C87). OpenEval finds support despite acknowledging lack of direct experimental evidence. Peer review identifies this as a key weakness, questioning how assembly-specific statistics reflect likelihoods and whether the mechanism is biologically necessary. Significant disagreement on adequacy of support.

Both address unified learning principle (C75-C76, C78). OpenEval finds support across multiple architectures. Peer review raises fundamental concern about lack of overarching optimization goal, questioning how different weight-specific rules achieve desired network dynamics. Major disagreement on theoretical coherence.

Both evaluate novelty claims (C79-C80, C92-C93). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN due to difficulty verifying 'first' claims. Peer review explicitly marks as UNSUPPORTED, stating claims are 'not consistent with the literature' and directly refuting novelty assertions. Both skeptical, but peer review more definitive in rejection.
Perfect overlap on background literature claims (C1-C2, C10-C12, C72-C74). Both evaluations confirm these are established, appropriately cited foundational concepts. Complete agreement.

Both address comparisons with prior work (C82-C83, C80-C81, C89). OpenEval finds support for mathematical formulation and stability claims. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, noting some characterizations of previous models are 'not consistent with the literature.' Disagreement on accuracy of comparisons.

Both evaluate speculative implications (C9, C96-C97, C99-C101). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting these require additional validation. Peer review finds them appropriately framed as discussion points. Both accept these as speculative but reasonable.

OpenEval evaluates mechanism distinction from Markovian models (C28-C29, C35-C36, C40, C47). Peer review confirms basic assembly formation (C23-C26, C28-C29) without challenge. Partial overlap; both supportive of assembly formation results.

OpenEval addresses within-assembly dynamics and non-Markovian mechanism (C28-C29, C35-C36, C40, C47). Peer review treats C34 and C47 as confirmatory supporting results. Minimal overlap; both supportive of what they evaluate.

OpenEval evaluates model-experiment match (C8, C20, C94-C95) with acknowledgment of alternatives. Peer review confirms experimental link (C55-C59, C94-C95) as strength. Both supportive with appropriate caveats about alternative mechanisms.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about prior computational work (C3, C13-C16) establishing gaps the study addresses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer review does challenge some characterizations of prior work elsewhere.

OpenEval confirms cited experimental/computational findings (C77, C81, C89, C98, C100-C101). Peer review addresses subset (C80-C83, C89) with uncertainty about accuracy of prior work characterizations. Partial overlap with some disagreement on comparison accuracy.

OpenEval validates cited findings and connections to neuroscience/ML concepts (C77, C81, C89, C98, C100-C101). Peer review addresses speculative implications (C96-C97, C99-C101). Minimal overlap; both accept speculative framing where overlap exists.
